The large-limit DoS concern is plausible but secondary.

judged_text: members passes user-controlled (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and params[:offset].to_i straight into .limit/.offset with no bounds validation, and this diff newly applies user-controlled pagination to every group rather than only automatic ones. Any user who can see a group can hit GET /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 (or limit=-1) and get a Postgres 'OFFSET must not be negative' 500 on the public endpoint (error-log noise and cheap error-tracking spam), and an arbitrarily large limit serializes the entire membership of huge groups in a single response.

Any user who can see a group can hit GET /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 (or limit=-1) and get a Postgres 'OFFSET must not be negative' 500 on the public endpoint (error-log noise and cheap error-tracking spam), and an arbitrarily large limit serializes the entire membership of huge groups in a single response.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff now unconditionally applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` for all groups, and feeds them directly into `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no bounds checks. Since `to_i` allows negative and arbitrarily large values, a request like `?offset=-1` can propagate a negative OFFSET to SQL (Postgres rejects negative OFFSET), causing a 500 on this public endpoint. Likewise a very large (or potentially `-1`) limit can cause overly large responses / load by serializing huge group memberships in one request. This risk is directly visible in the new code and is a behavior change from the prior conditional pagination for automatic groups only.
